cases.sentence: Он съездил к графу Растопчину, к некоторым знакомым, вернувшимся в Москву и собирался на ___ ехать в Петербург.
cases.explain: «третий день» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: At the end of January Pierre went to Moscow and stayed in an annex of his house which had not been burned. He called on Count Rostopchín and on some acquaintances who were back in Moscow, and he intended to leave for Petersburg two days later. Everybody was celebrating the victory, everything was bubbling with life in the ruined but reviving city. Everyone was pleased to see Pierre, everyone wished to meet him, and everyone questioned him about what he had seen. Pierre felt particularly well disposed toward them all, but was now instinctively on his guard for fear of binding himself in any way. To all questions put to him—whether important or quite trifling—such as: Where would he live? Was he going to rebuild? When was he going to Petersburg and would he mind taking a parcel for someone?—he replied: “Yes, perhaps,” or, “I think so,” and so on.

cases.sentence: Ежели она и приходила, то только как ___ давно прошедшего.
cases.explain: «приятное воспоминание» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: He had heard that the Rostóvs were at Kostromá but the thought of Natásha seldom occurred to him. If it did it was only as a pleasant memory of the distant past. He felt himself not only free from social obligations but also from that feeling which, it seemed to him, he had aroused in himself.

cases.sentence: Он чувствовал себя не только свободным от ___, но и от этого чувства, которое он, как ему казалось, умышленно напустил на себя.
cases.explain: «житейских условий» — after the preposition «от», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: He had heard that the Rostóvs were at Kostromá but the thought of Natásha seldom occurred to him. If it did it was only as a pleasant memory of the distant past. He felt himself not only free from social obligations but also from that feeling which, it seemed to him, he had aroused in himself.

cases.sentence: На ___ своего приезда в Москву, он узнал от Друбецких, что княжна Марья в Москве.
cases.explain: «третий день» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: On the third day after his arrival he heard from the Drubetskóys that Princess Márya was in Moscow. The death, sufferings, and last days of Prince Andréy had often occupied Pierre’s thoughts and now recurred to him with fresh vividness. Having heard at dinner that Princess Márya was in Moscow and living in her house—which had not been burned—in Vozdvízhenka Street, he drove that same evening to see her.

cases.sentence: Смерть, страдания, ___ князя Андрея, часто занимали Пьера, и теперь, с новою живостью, пришли ему в голову.
cases.explain: «последние дни» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.

cases.sentence: «Неужели он умер в том ___, в котором он был тогда?
cases.explain: «злобном настроении» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “Is it possible that he died in the bitter frame of mind he was then in? Is it possible that the meaning of life was not disclosed to him before he died?” thought Pierre. He recalled Karatáev and his death and involuntarily began to compare these two men, so different, and yet so similar in that they had both lived and both died and in the love he felt for both of them.

cases.sentence: В самом серьезном расположении духа Пьер подъехал к дому ___.
cases.explain: «старого князя» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Pierre drove up to the house of the old prince in a most serious mood. The house had escaped the fire; it showed signs of damage but its general aspect was unchanged. The old footman, who met Pierre with a stern face as if wishing to make the visitor feel that the absence of the old prince had not disturbed the order of things in the house, informed him that the princess had gone to her own apartments, and that she received on Sundays.

cases.sentence: Встретивший Пьера ___ с строгим лицом, как будто желая дать почувствовать гостю, что отсутствие князя не нарушает порядка дома, сказал, что княжна изволила пройти в свои комнаты и принимает по воскресеньям.
cases.explain: «старый официант» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.

cases.sentence: В ___, освещенной одною свечей, сидела княжна и еще кто-то с ней, в черном платье.
cases.explain: «невысокой комнатке» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: In a rather low room lit by one candle sat the princess and with her another person dressed in black. Pierre remembered that the princess always had lady companions, but who they were and what they were like he never knew or remembered. “This must be one of her companions,” he thought, glancing at the lady in the black dress.

cases.sentence: Это было единственное ___, которое мы получили с давнего времени.
cases.explain: «радостное известие» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “I was so glad to hear of your safety. It was the first piece of good news we had received for a long time.” Again the princess glanced round at her companion with even more uneasiness in her manner and was about to add something, but Pierre interrupted her.
